2609.11877.title: Biology-in-the-loop: Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens
2609.11877.paper_summary: Many biological discovery problems require experiments to be selected sequentially under constrained budgets. CRISPR screening is a prominent example, as exhaustive perturbation testing is often infeasible and candidate perturbations must instead be prioritized over multiple experimental rounds. Despite the importance of this problem, existing benchmarks for adaptive hit discovery remain limited in scale and diversity. Here, we introduce AssayBench-Loop, a large-scale benchmark for adaptive hit discovery comprising 1,389 CRISPR screens across five phenotype categories. Beyond enabling systematic evaluation, its scale makes it possible to learn acquisition strategies across historical experiments. Building on this resource, we introduce AssayLoop, a sequential experimental design framework combining AssayFormer, a transformer-based amortized acquisition policy trained across historical screens to adapt from experimental feedback, with LLM-derived biological priors through an adaptive handoff. In this view, completed experiments become training data for learning how accumulated evidence should guide what to test next, while LLMs provide prior biological knowledge to seed the search. We further introduce AssayLLM, showing that the same principle can be extended directly to an LLM through task-specific post-training. On temporally held-out screens, AssayLoop achieves a 5.67-fold enrichment over random selection and recovers 27.7% of hits after assaying approximately 5% of the candidate library, outperforming existing adaptive-design methods and standalone LLMs, and AssayFormer alone. Performance improves with increasing historical training data and transfers to phenotype categories excluded from training. These results demonstrate the value of learning acquisition policies across historical experiments and combining them with broad biological priors for efficient adaptive hit discovery.
2609.11877.paper_summary_zh: 許多生物發現問題需要在有限預算下依序選擇實驗。CRISPR篩選是一個突出的例子，因為全面的擾動測試通常不可行，候選擾動必須在多個實驗回合中優先考慮。儘管這個問題的重要性，現有的自適應命中發現基準在規模和多樣性上仍然有限。在此，我們介紹AssayBench-Loop，一個大規模的自適應命中發現基準，包含1,389個CRISPR篩選，涵蓋五個表型類別。除了能夠進行系統評估之外，其規模使得可以學習歷史實驗中的獲取策略。在這個資源的基礎上，我們介紹AssayLoop，一個結合AssayFormer的序列實驗設計框架，這是一種基於Transformer的攤銷獲取政策，通過歷史篩選進行訓練以適應實驗反饋，並通過自適應交接結合LLM衍生的生物先驗知識。在這個觀點下，已完成的實驗成為學習如何指導下一步測試的累積證據的訓練數據，而LLM則提供先驗的生物知識以啟動搜索。我們進一步介紹AssayLLM，顯示同樣的原則可以通過任務特定的後期訓練直接擴展到LLM。在時間上保留的篩選中，AssayLoop在隨機選擇上實現了5.67倍的富集，並在對約5%的候選庫進行測試後恢復了27.7%的命中，超越了現有的自適應設計方法和獨立的LLM，以及僅使用AssayFormer。隨著歷史訓練數據的增加，性能有所提升，並能轉移到排除在訓練之外的表型類別。這些結果展示了在歷史實驗中學習獲取政策的價值，並將其與廣泛的生物先驗知識結合，以實現高效的自適應命中發現。
